#Extended API and private channels

The extended bot API is shipped. It adds private text channels, category and channel management, message editing and bulk tools, pins and reactions, richer member and role tools, audit log reads, server settings, and webhook management. Everything is versioned under /api/v1.

This page is the deep reference for those surfaces. The API reference covers the core message and gateway contract, and Webhooks covers posting through a webhook URL.

#Authentication

Every endpoint uses the bot token:

Authorization: Bot <token>
Content-Type: application/json

A missing, invalid, or revoked token returns:

{ "error": "Invalid bot token" }

with status 401. There is no unauthenticated read path in this API.

#Scopes

A bot has an account-level scope list chosen when it is created (and editable by its owner), plus a per-space grant approved when the bot joins that space. The effective scopes are the intersection of the two.

Lowering a bot's account scopes applies immediately: the removed scopes are trimmed from every existing space grant. Adding a scope back does not restore old grants; the bot has to be approved for that scope again.

Scope What it unlocks
messages.read Gateway message events, message history, channel and category lists, channel detail, pinned messages
messages.write Send and edit messages and pin messages
messages.delete Delete messages, bulk delete, unpin messages, edit messages
messages.react Add and remove the bot's reactions
members.read Member list, member detail, role list
members.kick Kick members
members.ban Ban, unban, and list bans
members.timeout Time out members
channels.read Channel and category lists, channel detail, channel permission list
channels.manage Create, update, reorder, and delete channels and categories; set channel overwrites
webhooks.manage List, create, update, and delete webhooks
roles.manage Create, edit, and delete roles; assign and remove roles; manage channel overwrites
servers.read Read a space's name, description, icon, banner, and member count
audit.read Read the audit log

Earlier drafts of this page used colon names such as channels:read and messages:send. Those names were never accepted in production. Use the dotted names above.

#The two authorization gates

Most write endpoints require both:

  1. the relevant scope, granted on the bot and in that space, and
  2. a role permission on the bot's account in that space.

For example, creating a channel needs channels.manage and the manage_channels role permission. A bot with the scope but not the role permission gets 403.

Reads are usually scope-only. A few read endpoints also accept a role permission as an alternative; those exceptions are called out below.

Every check is deny-by-default and runs against the bot's real account, roles, and channel overwrites. Client-supplied role IDs or permission flags are never trusted.

#Private text channels

There is no visibility column and no separate private-channel object. A private channel is a normal text channel with role permission overwrites in channel_permissions.

#Overwrite fields

Field Meaning
can_view See the channel, its metadata, and its messages
can_post Send messages
can_react Add reactions
can_attach Upload attachments

Each field is true (allow), false (deny), or null (inherit).

#How to make a channel private

  1. Deny can_view for the @everyone role.
  2. Allow can_view for each staff or participant role that should see it.

@everyone is the default role in the space — the role with is_default: true in GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/roles.

curl -X POST https://www.disband.dev/api/v1/servers/SERVER_ID/channels \
  -H "Authorization: Bot $DISBAND_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "staff-chat",
    "type": "text",
    "permissions": [
      { "role_id": "EVERYONE_ROLE_ID", "can_view": false },
      { "role_id": "STAFF_ROLE_ID", "can_view": true, "can_post": true }
    ]
  }'

Notes:

  • role_id in channel creation must be a role UUID. Use the id field from GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/roles.
  • Up to 100 overwrites can be supplied when creating a channel.
  • A role used in an overwrite must sit below the bot's highest role.
  • @everyone is always allowed as an overwrite target.

#Viewing rules

  • Access is evaluated per role. If any role assigned to the member (including @everyone) allows the permission, the member has it. A false overwrite on one role does not veto another role's true; it only withholds that role's grant.
  • For can_view, a role with no row inherits the @everyone overwrite. If @everyone has no row either, it is allowed.
  • For can_post, can_react, and can_attach, a role with no overwrite falls back to that role's server permissions (send_messages, add_reactions, attach_files).
  • If a channel has no overwrites at all, every member can view it and posting is governed by the normal server permissions and read_only.
  • The space owner, members with Administrator, and members with the manage_channels role permission bypass channel overwrites and can always view every channel. This is intentional: space managers can always audit what is in their space.
  • A channel with read_only: true blocks posting for everyone except the bypasses above. It does not block reading.

#What a bot without access sees

  • GET /servers/{id}/channels silently omits channels the bot cannot view.
  • GET /channels/{id} returns 404 and the message Channel not found.
  • Message reads and writes return 403 with Channel permission denied.
  • Gateway events are only queued for channels the bot can view. A private channel's events never reach a bot that cannot see it.

Treat both 403 and 404 as "not available to this bot"; do not build logic that depends on the exact status for a hidden channel.

#No category-level permissions

Production has no category_permissions table. Categories are for display and ordering only. Channel-level overwrites are authoritative. Do not design an integration around inheriting permissions from a category — it does not happen.

#Bot access to the channels it creates

A bot follows the same overwrite rules as everyone else. If it creates a channel that denies @everyone and does not allow a role the bot has, the bot will not be able to read or post in its own new channel. Either:

  • give the bot's highest role can_view: true in the new channel, or
  • give the bot a role with manage_channels / Administrator (which bypasses overwrites).

POST /servers/{id}/channels still returns 201 with the new channel_id in this case; channel may be null because the follow-up detail read is denied.

#Ticket systems

Disband deliberately does not implement ticket objects, claiming, or transcripts in the API. It exposes the primitives a ticket bot needs:

  • categories and channels,
  • private channels with role overwrites,
  • roles and member role assignment,
  • messages, embeds, buttons, and interactions,
  • audit logging.

A typical private ticket flow:

  1. Find or create a category for tickets (GET/POST /servers/{id}/categories).
  2. Create a per-ticket role with POST /servers/{id}/roles (requires roles.manage + manage_roles). The role must sit below the bot's highest role.
  3. Assign that role to the opener with PUT /servers/{id}/members/{user_id}/roles/{role_id}. The target must be below the bot's highest role and must not be the space owner.
  4. Create the ticket channel with can_view: false for @everyone, can_view: true for the ticket role, and can_view: true for the staff role. Include the bot's own role if the bot does not have manage_channels.
  5. Post the ticket panel with a message containing buttons. Button presses arrive on the gateway as interactionCreate events; answer them through the interaction callback endpoint.
  6. Close the ticket by deleting the channel and the per-ticket role.

Every ticket role counts toward the 250 roles per space limit. Plan for that: a role-per-ticket design supports roughly 249 simultaneously open tickets (plus the @everyone role and any permanent staff roles). If you need more, reuse a smaller set of staff channels rather than one channel per ticket.

For private staff channels, skip the per-ticket role: deny @everyone, and allow the existing staff role. That costs no extra roles.

#Endpoint reference

All paths are relative to https://www.disband.dev.

#Servers

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id} Any of servers.read, messages.read, channels.read, channels.manage, members.read —
PATCH /api/v1/servers/{server_id} Any granted scope manage_server
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/permissions Any granted scope —

GET returns server metadata plus member_count:

{
  "server": {
    "id": "…",
    "name": "Space",
    "description": "…",
    "icon_url": "…",
    "banner_url": null,
    "owner_id": "…",
    "created_at": "…",
    "discoverable": true,
    "verified": false,
    "member_count": 42
  }
}

PATCH accepts name, description, and discoverable:

{ "name": "New name", "description": "New description", "discoverable": true }

Unknown fields are rejected with 400. The bot must be a member of the space; otherwise the response is 403.

GET /permissions is a self-check endpoint. It returns the bot's granted scopes, its role IDs, its highest role position, and a map of the role permissions it currently holds:

{
  "server_id": "…",
  "user_id": "…",
  "scopes": ["messages.read", "channels.manage"],
  "permissions": {
    "add_reactions": true,
    "attach_files": true,
    "ban": false,
    "create_invites": true,
    "kick": false,
    "manage_channels": true,
    "manage_emojis": false,
    "manage_messages": false,
    "manage_roles": false,
    "manage_server": false,
    "manage_webhooks": false,
    "mention_everyone": false,
    "pin_messages": false,
    "send_messages": true,
    "timeout_members": false,
    "view_audit_log": false
  },
  "highest_role_position": 3,
  "roles": ["…"]
}

#Categories

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/categories Any of messages.read, channels.read, channels.manage —
POST /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/categories channels.manage manage_channels
PATCH /api/v1/categories/{category_id} channels.manage manage_channels
DELETE /api/v1/categories/{category_id} channels.manage manage_channels

GET returns categories ordered by position. channel_count counts only the channels the bot can view, so private channels are not leaked through it:

{
  "categories": [
    { "id": "…", "server_id": "…", "name": "Text Channels", "position": 0, "channel_count": 2 }
  ]
}

POST body: { "name": "Support" }. Returns 201 with { "category": { … } }.

PATCH body: { "name": "Renamed", "position": 2 }. Position is a zero-based whole number. Returns { "category": { … } }.

DELETE returns 204. Its channels become uncategorized; they are not deleted.

#Channels

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/channels Any of messages.read, channels.read, channels.manage —
POST /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/channels channels.manage manage_channels
GET /api/v1/channels/{channel_id} Any of messages.read, channels.read, channels.manage —
PATCH /api/v1/channels/{channel_id} channels.manage manage_channels
DELETE /api/v1/channels/{channel_id} channels.manage manage_channels

GET /servers/{id}/channels returns only channels the bot can view, ordered by position. Each channel includes effective can_post, can_react, can_attach, and can_manage flags:

{
  "channels": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "server_id": "…",
      "category_id": "…",
      "category_name": "Text Channels",
      "name": "general",
      "type": "text",
      "position": 0,
      "topic": "…",
      "slow_mode_seconds": 0,
      "read_only": false,
      "locked": false,
      "is_stage": false,
      "user_limit": null,
      "created_at": "…",
      "can_post": true,
      "can_react": true,
      "can_attach": true,
      "can_manage": false
    }
  ]
}

POST body:

{
  "name": "staff-only",
  "type": "text",
  "category_id": null,
  "topic": "Staff discussion",
  "slow_mode_seconds": 0,
  "read_only": false,
  "user_limit": null,
  "permissions": [
    { "role_id": "@everyone-uuid", "can_view": false },
    { "role_id": "staff-uuid", "can_view": true, "can_post": true }
  ]
}
  • type is text or voice (default text).
  • Names are trimmed, lowercased, and limited to 100 characters.
  • Topics are up to 1,024 characters.
  • slow_mode_seconds is 0–21,600.
  • user_limit is 0–99 for voice channels, or null.
  • permissions is optional, up to 100 role overwrites.
  • Returns 201 with { "channel_id": "…", "channel": { … } }.
  • channel can be null if creating the overwrites made the channel invisible to the bot; see "Bot access to the channels it creates".

GET /channels/{id} returns { "channel": { … } } with the same fields plus can_view: true and, when the bot has manage_channels, a permissions array:

{
  "permissions": [
    {
      "role_id": "…",
      "role_name": "@everyone",
      "can_view": false,
      "can_post": null,
      "can_react": null,
      "can_attach": null
    }
  ]
}

PATCH accepts any of name, topic, slow_mode_seconds, category_id, position, read_only, locked, user_limit, and type:

{ "name": "deploys-2", "topic": null, "slow_mode_seconds": 10, "position": 1 }
  • type is accepted only if it equals the current type; channels cannot change type.
  • category_id may be a category UUID or null.
  • Unknown fields return 400.
  • Returns { "channel": { … } }.

DELETE removes the channel and its messages, then returns 204. This is audited.

#Channel permission overwrites

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/permissions Any of channels.read, channels.manage, roles.manage —
PUT /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/permissions/{role_id} channels.manage or roles.manage manage_channels
DELETE /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/permissions/{role_id} channels.manage or roles.manage manage_channels

GET returns the raw overwrite rows, highest role first:

{
  "permissions": [
    { "role_id": "…", "can_view": false, "can_post": null, "can_react": null, "can_attach": null }
  ]
}

PUT body — every field is optional and defaults to null:

{ "can_view": true, "can_post": true, "can_react": null, "can_attach": null }

true allows, false denies, and null clears the override. Returns { "ok": true }.

DELETE clears the role's row entirely, so it inherits again. Returns { "ok": true }.

role_id may be a role UUID or a numeric role display_id on these two routes. The role must be below the bot's highest role, except @everyone.

#Messages

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages messages.read —
POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages messages.write send_messages
PATCH /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id} messages.write or messages.delete manage_messages to edit someone else's
DELETE /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id} messages.delete manage_messages to delete someone else's
POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages/bulk-delete messages.delete manage_messages to delete someone else's

GET query: limit (1–100, default 50) and before (a message UUID for backwards paging). Returns { "messages": [ … ] }, newest first.

POST body:

{
  "content": "Deploy finished",
  "reply_to_id": null,
  "embeds": [],
  "components": []
}
  • content is required unless embeds is non-empty.
  • Content is up to 4,000 characters.
  • Up to 10 embeds; see Embeds.
  • Up to 5 action rows of 5 buttons; see the button schema below.
  • @everyone / @here needs the mention_everyone role permission.
  • Returns 201 with { "message": { … } }.

PATCH accepts content, embeds, and components. Omitting a field leaves it unchanged; sending null for embeds or components clears it. A bot can edit its own messages; editing someone else's needs manage_messages. Returns { "message": { … } }.

DELETE returns 204. A bot can always delete its own messages; deleting someone else's needs manage_messages.

POST /messages/bulk-delete body:

{ "message_ids": ["uuid", "uuid"] }
  • 1–100 UUIDs. Numeric display_id values are not accepted here.
  • Duplicates, unknown IDs, and IDs from other channels are ignored; the response reports how many rows were actually deleted: { "deleted": 12 }.
  • Deleting someone else's messages needs manage_messages.

message_id in the single-message routes may be a UUID or the numeric display_id shown in the app.

#Reactions

Method Path Scope Role permission
PUT /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id}/reactions/{emoji} messages.react add_reactions
DELETE /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id}/reactions/{emoji} messages.react add_reactions

{emoji} is URL-encoded and 1–32 characters. Both routes manage only the bot's own reaction. PUT is idempotent and returns:

{ "reaction": { "id": "…", "message_id": "…", "emoji": "✅" } }

DELETE is idempotent and returns { "removed": true } or { "removed": false } if the reaction was not there.

#Pins

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/pins Any of messages.read, channels.read, channels.manage —
PUT /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/pins/{message_id} messages.write or messages.delete pin_messages
DELETE /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/pins/{message_id} messages.write or messages.delete pin_messages

GET returns pinned messages, newest pin first:

{
  "pins": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "message_id": "…",
      "content": "…",
      "author_id": "…",
      "author": { "id": "…", "username": "…", "display_name": "…", "avatar_url": "…", "is_bot": false },
      "pinned_by": "…",
      "created_at": "…",
      "message": { "…": "the full message, or null if it was deleted" }
    }
  ]
}

PUT is idempotent and returns { "pin": { "id": "…", "message_id": "…", "channel_id": "…" } }. DELETE is idempotent and returns { "removed": true } or { "removed": false }.

#Members

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/members members.read —
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/members/{user_id} members.read —
DELETE /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/members/{user_id} members.kick —
PATCH /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/members/{user_id} members.timeout —
PUT /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/members/{user_id}/roles/{role_id} roles.manage manage_roles
DELETE /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/members/{user_id}/roles/{role_id} roles.manage manage_roles

GET list returns members sorted by display name:

{
  "members": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "username": "…",
      "display_name": "…",
      "avatar_url": "…",
      "is_bot": false,
      "status": "online",
      "role": "member",
      "roles": ["role-uuid"],
      "joined_at": "…"
    }
  ]
}

GET one returns profile details, roles, highest role position, and any active timeout:

{
  "member": {
    "id": "…",
    "username": "…",
    "display_name": "…",
    "avatar_url": "…",
    "bio": "…",
    "status": "online",
    "is_bot": false,
    "is_owner": false,
    "joined_at": "…",
    "role": "member",
    "roles": [{ "id": "…", "name": "Staff", "color": "#5865f2", "position": 3, "is_default": false }],
    "highest_role_position": 3,
    "timed_out_until": null
  }
}

DELETE kicks the member and returns { "ok": true }.

PATCH times a member out:

{ "timeout_minutes": 10, "reason": "Cooling off" }
  • timeout_minutes is required and must be 1–40,320 (28 days).
  • Returns { "ok": true, "timed_out_until": "2026-11-11T12:00:00Z" }.

Kicks and timeouts protect the space owner, moderators (anyone with kick, ban, or manage_server), bots, and the calling bot itself.

Role assignment:

  • The role must be below the bot's highest role.
  • The target member must be below the bot's highest role.
  • The target cannot be the space owner.
  • @everyone cannot be given or taken.
  • Both routes return { "ok": true } and are idempotent.

role_id may be a UUID or numeric display_id.

#Bans

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/bans members.ban, or the ban role permission —
PUT /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/bans/{user_id} members.ban —
DELETE /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/bans/{user_id} members.ban ban

GET returns bans, newest first:

{
  "bans": [
    { "user_id": "…", "banned_by": "…", "reason": "…", "created_at": "…" }
  ]
}

PUT body is optional: { "reason": "…" } (up to 500 characters). Returns { "ok": true }. The same target protections as kick apply.

DELETE unbans and returns { "removed": true } or { "removed": false }. Unlike PUT, unban requires the ban role permission as well as the scope.

#Roles

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/roles roles.manage or members.read —
POST /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/roles roles.manage manage_roles
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/roles/{role_id} roles.manage or members.read —
PATCH /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/roles/{role_id} roles.manage manage_roles
DELETE /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/roles/{role_id} roles.manage manage_roles

Roles are returned highest first and include a manageable flag:

{
  "roles": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "display_id": "383216538525554",
      "name": "Staff",
      "color": "#5865f2",
      "position": 3,
      "permissions": { "send_messages": true, "manage_messages": true },
      "is_default": false,
      "self_assignable": false,
      "manageable": true
    }
  ]
}

Create body:

{
  "name": "Ticket Staff",
  "color": "#5865f2",
  "permissions": { "send_messages": true, "add_reactions": true },
  "self_assignable": false,
  "position": 2
}
  • name is required (1–100 characters).
  • color is a hex colour like #5865f2. Omitted or null uses the default grey on create and leaves the current colour on edit.
  • permissions is an object of permission names to booleans. Omitted keys are false on create. On edit the map is merged, so omitted keys keep their current value.
  • position is 1 or greater and must be below the bot's highest role.
  • A space can have at most 250 roles.
  • Returns 201 with { "role": { … } }.

Permission keys:

add_reactions, attach_files, ban, create_invites, kick, manage_channels, manage_emojis, manage_messages, manage_roles, manage_server, manage_webhooks, mention_everyone, pin_messages, send_messages, timeout_members, view_audit_log.

PATCH accepts name, color, permissions, self_assignable, and position; omitted fields stay unchanged. permissions is merged into the existing map, so omitted keys keep their current value. @everyone cannot be edited or deleted. Returns { "role": { … } }.

DELETE returns { "ok": true }. role_id may be a UUID or numeric display_id.

#Audit log

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/audit audit.read, or the view_audit_log role permission —

Unlike most endpoints, this one accepts either the scope or the role permission. Query limit is 1–100 (default 100). Entries are newest first:

{
  "audit": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "server_id": "…",
      "actor_id": "…",
      "action": "channel.create",
      "target_type": "channel",
      "target_id": "…",
      "details": { "name": "staff-chat", "bot": "…" },
      "created_at": "…"
    }
  ]
}

Actions written by the extended API include:

category.create, category.update, category.delete, channel.create, channel.update, channel.delete, channel.permissions, message.edit, message.delete, message.bulk_delete, message.pin, message.unpin, member.kick, member.ban, member.unban, member.timeout, member.role_add, member.role_remove, role.create, role.update, role.delete, server.update, webhook.create, webhook.update, webhook.token_reset, webhook.delete, bot.invite.approve.

#Webhooks

Method Path Scope Role permission
GET /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/webhooks webhooks.manage manage_webhooks
POST /api/v1/servers/{server_id}/webhooks webhooks.manage manage_webhooks
GET /api/v1/webhooks/{webhook_id} webhooks.manage manage_webhooks
PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/{webhook_id} webhooks.manage manage_webhooks
DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/{webhook_id} webhooks.manage manage_webhooks

GET /servers/{id}/webhooks returns webhooks newest first. Every object includes its posting url. Treat that URL as a secret. Webhooks that live in a channel the bot cannot view are omitted; reading, moving, rotating, or deleting one of them returns 404.

{
  "webhooks": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "server_id": "…",
      "channel_id": "…",
      "name": "Deploys",
      "avatar_url": null,
      "url": "https://disband.dev/webhook/…/…",
      "created_at": "…",
      "last_used_at": null
    }
  ]
}

POST body:

{ "channel_id": "…", "name": "Deploys", "avatar_url": null }
  • channel_id is required and must be a text channel the bot can view.
  • name is optional (1–80 characters); a random name is used if omitted.
  • avatar_url must be an HTTPS image URL or null.
  • Returns 201 with { "webhook": { … } }.

GET /webhooks/{id} returns { "webhook": { … } }.

PATCH body:

{ "name": "New name", "avatar_url": null, "channel_id": "…", "reset_token": true }
  • channel_id must be a visible text channel in the same space.
  • reset_token: true rotates the URL; the old URL stops working immediately.
  • Returns the updated { "webhook": { … } }.

DELETE soft-deletes the webhook and returns 204. Messages it already posted remain.

Limits: 50 webhooks per space, 15 per channel. Webhook sends are rate limited separately at the public webhook URL.

#Gateway

GET /api/v1/gateway?timeout=20

The gateway is a long-poll. timeout is clamped to 1–20 seconds; the request returns as soon as events are available.

Event types:

Type Delivered when
messageCreate A message is posted in a channel the bot can view
messageUpdate A message in a visible channel is edited
messageDelete A message in a visible channel is deleted
memberJoin Someone joins a space the bot is in (members.read in that space)
memberLeave Someone leaves a space the bot is in (members.read in that space)
memberUpdate A member's roles change (members.read in that space)
interactionCreate Someone runs the bot's slash command or presses its button

Message events require messages.read on both the bot and the space grant. Member events require members.read on the space grant. Interaction events require the bot to be in the space. Delivery is at-least-once: handle events idempotently by event ID.

#Slash commands

Method Path Scope
GET /api/v1/commands Any authenticated bot
PUT /api/v1/commands Any authenticated bot
POST /api/v1/commands Any authenticated bot
DELETE /api/v1/commands?name=weather Any authenticated bot

Commands are global to the bot: every space the bot is in offers them.

{
  "name": "weather",
  "description": "Show the forecast",
  "options": [
    { "name": "city", "description": "City name", "type": "string", "required": true }
  ]
}
  • Command names are 1–32 lowercase letters, digits, _, or -.
  • Descriptions are 1–100 characters.
  • Up to 25 options per command; option types are string, integer, number, boolean, user, channel, and role.
  • Required options must come before optional ones.
  • Up to 100 commands per bot.
  • PUT replaces the whole list (bulk overwrite); POST creates or updates one by name; DELETE needs ?name=.

#Interactions

POST /api/v1/interactions/{interaction_id}/callback

Answer a slash command or button press within 15 minutes:

{
  "content": "Here is the forecast",
  "embeds": [],
  "components": [],
  "update": false,
  "ephemeral": false
}
  • update: true edits the message the button is on instead of posting a reply.
  • ephemeral: true (or Discord's flags: 64) shows the reply only to the person who ran the command.
  • Up to 5 answers per interaction.
  • Answering does not require messages.write; the member invoked the bot directly.

The interactionCreate payload contains the interaction id, type (command or component), server_id, channel_id, the invoking user, and either command: { name, options } or component: { custom_id, message_id }.

#Invites

POST /api/v1/bots/{bot_id}/invites

{ "server_id": "…", "scopes": ["messages.read", "channels.manage"] }
  • The token must belong to that bot.
  • The requested scopes must be a subset of the bot's account scopes and must be valid scope names.
  • The caller must be a member of the target space.
  • Returns { "code": "…", "invite_url": "…" }. Invites expire after 7 days.
  • Rate limit: 10 per minute per bot.

General install links are created by the bot owner from the developers portal or POST /api/bot/install-link; they are reusable and let the recipient pick a space they manage.

#Rate limits

Limits are per bot token and persist across server instances. The in-memory limiter is a burst pre-filter; the database enforces the full window.

Bucket Limit
Gateway long-poll 15 requests per minute
Reads 120 per minute
Writes 60 per minute
Invite creation 10 per minute
Bot registration 10 per day per owner

A limited request returns 429 with a Retry-After header and a JSON error. Honour the header rather than retrying immediately.

The database also enforces:

  • 4,000 characters per message,
  • 100 permission overwrites per channel,
  • 250 roles per space,
  • 100 slash commands per bot,
  • 50 webhooks per space and 15 per channel,
  • 1–100 messages per bulk delete,
  • 1–28 days per timeout,
  • 500-character ban and timeout reasons.

#Errors

All errors are JSON:

{ "error": "Human-readable message" }
Status Meaning
400 Invalid input, unknown field, malformed ID, or limit exceeded
401 Missing, invalid, or revoked bot token
403 Missing scope or grant, missing role permission, hierarchy violation, read-only channel, or restricted bot
404 Resource missing or not visible to the bot
429 Rate limited; honour Retry-After
500 Internal error; retry with backoff
503 Event delivery temporarily unavailable (gateway only)

Some hidden resources return 403 and some return 404. This is intentional in places to avoid leaking whether a channel exists, but it is not perfectly uniform. Treat both as "not available".

#Security model

  • Deny by default. Every request starts with no access. Access is added only by the bot's scopes, the space grant, and the bot account's roles.
  • Two gates. Account scopes alone are not enough; the space owner must also grant the scope. Role permissions are a third gate for management actions.
  • Central checks. Every route authenticates with the same bot-token lookup and every database RPC re-checks the bot's membership, scopes, and role permissions. A route cannot bypass the RPC checks by passing a different ID.
  • No direct table access. Bot tokens are not Supabase keys. All reads and writes go through the service-role RPCs and route handlers.
  • Hierarchy. Bots can only manage roles below their own highest role, and cannot kick, ban, time out, or edit the roles of the owner, moderators, other bots, or themselves.
  • Secrets. Bot tokens are hashed at rest and shown once. Webhook URLs are secrets; anyone with the URL can post. reset_token rotates them.
  • Audit. Management and moderation mutations write an audit row with the actor, action, target, and a small details object. The actor is the bot's user account; the details include the bot ID where useful. Reactions are not audited; message edits, single and bulk deletes, pins, and all channel, category, role, member, server, and webhook management changes are.
  • Visibility. Channel lists, channel detail, messages, pins, reactions, and gateway events all check can_view. Private channel contents do not leak to bots or members who cannot see the channel.

#Migrating from the pre-release draft

If you built against the earlier "planned" version of this page:

  • Scope names are dotted (messages.write, channels.manage, audit.read), not colon-separated.
  • Private channels use channel_permissions overwrites; there is no visibility: "private" field and no category_permissions table.
  • POST /channels returns { "channel_id", "channel" }, not just a bare ID.
  • PATCH and DELETE return the updated resource or 204, not { "success": true }.
  • Webhook management lives under /servers/{id}/webhooks and /webhooks/{id}, not /channels/{id}/webhooks.
  • Ticket endpoints do not exist. Use categories, private channels, roles, and interactions to build tickets.
